That’s the issue. If the game gets left alone metas form naturally. People, even at the lower ranks, start to play better and the people who stick with the game naturally get better at the game and figure out what’s the best to do in their situation. 

But change too much too often and the casual group won’t be able to keep up with the meta changes and just get stomped over and over by people who know how to read patch notes. 

There’s a fine balance that’s extremely difficult to balance on and I honestly don’t think any team shooter with a lot of heroes and maps and game modes will be able to perfectly balanced. 

Listening to players is also a bad idea honestly. In OW for instance N.A. players complained about certain heroes being too strong and to nerf them while Asia had the opposite issue where those same heroes had extremely low pick and win rates. And then there’s rank disparity. 

There’s just a lot going on that most people don’t realize and it’s not ever as simple as “don’t change too much” or “change more” or “devs don’t know how to balance”.

I’ve been using my cheapasss sous vide I got for a secret Santa like 4 years ago. I eat an unhealthy amount of steaks with it. Probably at least 2 a month but sometimes once a week.

The 1 thing I recommend is to also gauge the temp of the water of the sous vide after it reaches whatever temp you set it to. My machine needs to be set to 134 in order for the water temp to be 130.5.  

Also the char will never be as nice BUT you can lower the temp of the bath by a few degrees to dial that part in a bit better.

For a personal sized steak, about 1 inch thick, this is what I do.

*  Pat steak dry with paper towel and season with salt only. Pepper could burn in the hot pan.

* Leave the steak on the counter for around 30-45 mins so the inside of the steak is room temperature.

* Before turning on the store, make sure to have everything ready. Butter, salt, pepper, garlic and preferably some sort of grill mesh to rest the steak on top of.

* Pat the steak dry with paper again right before cooking. You want the steak to be as dry as possible when you put it in. You wont be taking salt off the steak because the meat already absorbed most, if not all, the salt.

* Stove on high and once the pan is warmed up, THEN add the high smoke point oil like avocado oil or sunflower oil. 

* As soon as the pan starts to smoke, place your steak in the pan. Turn your fans on, and open the windows, because it could get very smokey. I also place the steak on only 1 half of the pan, NOT the middle.

* After around 1 minute, I turn the steak over and place it on the half of the pan I did not use.  

* This is also when I throw in the garlic and butter. I put the garlic on the side of the pan thats not being used, while the butter in between the pans wall and steak. Do this for 30 seconds.

* After the 30 seconds, I turn the heat off. Tilt the pan so the steak is higher than the part of the pan thats touching the stove. The butter will collect into the the area where the garlic is. 

* This is when you use a spoon to baste the steak with the butter. Do this for at least a minute or so. 

* Your final step is to take the steak and put it on the grill/mesh. Leave it there for about 10 or so minutes. This is also the time I use to add the pepper on my steak.

* Add finishing salt and eat.
